messages.author: 16bac0a0bbd38012
messages.subject: credible intervals spatial-temporal model
parts:
Hello,

I'm not sure how to get credible intervals for each year for each covariate in a spatial-temporal model. I can get credible intervals for each covariate, but there is a single interval for each covariate, rather than an interval for every year of the model for every covariate. I want to see each interval for each year because I want to know whether a given covariate is important in one year, unimportant in another, changes direction of coefficient sign year-to-year, etc.

Here is my code.

#spatial-temporal model
require(INLA)
datafile.final2$YearSeq <- as.numeric(as.factor(datafile.final2$Year))
NYear <- length(unique(datafile.final2$YearSeq))
max.edge<- diff(range(datafile.final2$x))/15

mesh2 <- inla.mesh.2d(boundary=list(list(ppt1, pt1)), max.edge=c(1,5)*max.edge, cutoff=200)
#plot(mesh2)
#see computational power required (bigger number=need more power)
mesh2$n


coords <- as.matrix(datafile.final2[,1:2])

spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh=mesh2, alpha=2)

A <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh2, loc=coords,group=datafile.final2$YearSeq,n.group = NYear)
dim(A)
time.index <- inla.spde.make.index("w", n.spde=spde$n.spde,n.group = NYear)
head(datafile.final2)
N <- nrow(datafile.final2)

X <- data.frame(Intercept=rep(1,N), datafile.final2$secchi.std, datafile.final2$Nit.std,datafile.final2$distance.to.edge.std,datafile.final2$distance.between.beds.std,datafile.final2$bath.std,datafile.final2$dIICconnector_4000.std,datafile.final2$dIICflux_6000.std)

colnames(X) <- c("Intercept","secchi.std","Nit.std", "distance.to.edge.std","distance.between.beds.std","bath.std","dIICconnector_4000.std","dIICflux_6000.std")


stack3 <- inla.stack(data=list(y=datafile.final2$pres, link=1,Ntrials=1),A=list(A,1),effects=list(w=time.index, X=as.data.frame(X)), tag="est")


hyper <- list(theta = list(prior="pc.prec", param=c(1,0.01)))

formula3 <- y ~ -1 + Intercept + secchi.std+ Nit.std  +distance.to.edge.std+distance.between.beds.std+bath.std+dIICconnector_4000.std+dIICflux_6000.std+f(w, model=spde,group=w.group,control.group = list(model="ar1",scale.model = T),hyper=hyper)

data = inla.stack.data(stack3)


starting.value <- inla(formula3, control.inla=list(reordering="metis",diagonal=100,strategy="gaussian",int.strategy="eb",cmin=0),family="zeroinflatedbinomial1",Ntrials=1, data=data, control.compute=list(dic=T,cpo=T,config=T),control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack3), compute=T, link=1, quantiles=c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)),control.fixed=list(prec.intercept = 0.1),verbose=T)

r3 <- starting.value

#credible intervals
#visualize mean and 95 credible interval for posteriors
Combined <- r3$summary.fixed[,c("mean","0.025quant","0.975quant")]
#each=7
#each refers to number of fixed effects
Combined$WhichModel <- rep(c(""), each=8)

Combined$WhichVariable <- rep(rownames(r3$summary.fixed), 1)
colnames(Combined) <- c("Mean","Lo","Up","WhichModel","WhichVariable")


#to rename facets
variable_names_facet <- c(
  'bath.std'="Bathymetry",
  'Intercept'="Intercept",
  'Nit.std'="% days ≥ 3 mg/l total nitrogen",
  'secchi.std'="% days < 0.65 m secchi",
  'distance.to.edge.std'="Dist from 0 cell to edge",
  'distance.between.beds.std'="Dist betw 1 cells of diff patches",
  'dIICconnector_4000.std'="Connector",
  'dIICflux_6000.std'="Flux"
)
str(Combined)
require(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot()
p <- p + geom_point(data=Combined, aes(x=WhichModel, y=Mean))

p <- p+geom_errorbar(data=Combined,aes(x=WhichModel,ymax=Up,ymin=Lo),width=0.2)

p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept=0,linetype=2)
p <- p+xlab("Parameters")+ylab("Values")
p <- p +theme(text=element_text(size=13))
p <- p + facet_wrap(~ WhichVariable, scales="free_y", labeller=as_labeller(variable_names_facet))
p <- p + theme(legend.position="none")
p

Thanks!

-Carrie

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] credible intervals spatial-temporal model
parts:
Hi,

since you have defined the model with basic "fixed effects" for the
covariates, there _is_ only one coefficient for each of them; each
effect is just
beta * z(location, time)
when z(loc,time) is a space-time varying covariate.
So if you want different beta_z for different time points, you need to
define the model differently. Precisely how depends on what model
structure you want to have (e.g. independent beta_z for each time
point, with model="iid", or with some temporal correlation, such as
model="ar1"). You can then use something like f(time, mycovariate,
model="iid") to have the mycovariate values as weights, to give a
model with mathematical interpretation
beta(time) * mycovariate(space, time)

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] credible intervals spatial-temporal model
parts:
No, you would need a separate f() component for each covariate for which you want to have the more complicated model. I would suggest starting with a much simpler model just to get some practice in how to specify inla models in general. There are examples on the r-inla.org webpages, and for spde models in particular, a link to to the online version of a book on spde models examples.

Finn

﻿No, you would need a separate f() component for each covariate for which you want to have the more complicated model. I would suggest starting with a much simpler model just to get some practice in how to specify inla models in general. There are examples on the r-inla.org webpages, and for spde models in particular, a link to to the online version of a book on spde models examples.

On Tue, May 31, 2022 at 4:49 PM Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi,

since you have defined the model with basic "fixed effects" for the
covariates, there _is_ only one coefficient for each of them; each
effect is just
  beta * z(location, time)
when z(loc,time) is a space-time varying covariate.
So if you want different beta_z for different time points, you need to
define the model differently. Precisely how depends on what model
structure you want to have (e.g. independent beta_z for each time
point, with model="iid", or with some temporal correlation, such as
model="ar1"). You can then use something like f(time, mycovariate,
model="iid") to have the mycovariate values as weights, to give a
model with mathematical interpretation
  beta(time) * mycovariate(space, time)

Finn
